chapters.title: Chapter 1: Why Alternative Data Matters in Quant Research

lessons.title: Alpha Decay and the Search for Edge: Why Traditional Data Isn't Enough

body.text: An edge is not a fact about a dataset. It is a fact about how many other desks are trading against the same dataset, at the same speed, right now.

children.text: In the last lesson you saw why traditional NSE and BSE data decays fast as a source of alpha: everyone reads the same quarterly result at the same time. This lesson makes that intuition precise. You will learn to think about an edge as something with a half-life, quantify how fast that half-life shrinks as a dataset gets crowded, and separate two very different reasons a strategy stops working, because only one of them is fixed by finding new data.
Modelling Decay: An Edge as an Exponential Curve

markDefs.definition: The rate at which a signal's excess return shrinks per unit of time, driven mainly by how many participants adopt the same data source and how easily the signal can be replicated.

children.text: A useful working model treats a signal's excess return as decaying exponentially from the moment it becomes known, or the moment enough capital starts trading on it. If a signal starts at an excess return of R0, its excess return at time t is approximately R0 multiplied by e raised to the power of negative lambda times t, where lambda is the
. A crowded, easily replicated signal has a high lambda and its edge halves in weeks. A niche signal that is hard to source or hard to process has a low lambda and can keep paying for years.

body.caption: Excess return R(t) at time t, given a starting excess return R0 and decay rate lambda. Higher lambda means faster crowding, faster decay.

body.title: Calculate the Decayed Excess Return
body.prompt: A signal starts with an excess return of 40 basis points per month. Its estimated decay rate lambda is 0.15 per month. Using R(t) = R0 x e^(-lambda x t), what is the excess return after 4 months, in basis points, rounded to one decimal place?
body.explanation: R(4) = 40 x e^(-0.15 x 4) = 40 x e^(-0.6) = 40 x 0.5488 = 21.95, which rounds to about 22.0 bps. In four months the signal has already lost close to half its original edge, purely from the passage of time and presumed crowding, before any change in the underlying business.

body.title: Stylized decay curves: a crowded signal vs a niche signal
body.xAxisLabel: Months since the signal became known

children.text: These curves are stylized, not measured from any specific fund's book, but the shape is the point. A simple momentum rule built purely on NSE closing prices sits on the steep curve, because thousands of retail algo strategies and prop desks can compute the exact same moving average from the exact same data feed. A signal built from a data source that only your desk has cleaned properly sits on the shallow curve, for a while.
What Actually Drives Lambda Up in Indian Markets

Three forces push decay rates higher for any signal built purely on traditional data. Algorithmic trading, most of it built on the same price, volume, and F&O data, now accounts for a large and growing share of order flow on NSE and BSE, so any pattern visible in price and volume gets tested by many desks almost immediately. SEBI's exchange-approved algo framework and colocation facilities mean speed differences between well-capitalized participants have narrowed, so being marginally faster is a weaker moat than it once was. And retail access to the same tools, screener.in for fundamentals, TradingView and broker platforms for technicals, and free F&O open interest data, has widened the pool of people capable of finding an obvious pattern the moment it appears.

body.caption: How crowding maps to decay speed across common Indian data sources

cells: Every broker terminal, every retail algo platform, every prop desk
Weeks: simple price-based rules are re-discovered almost as fast as they are found
Quarterly ratios from screener.in (P/E, P/B, ROE)
Any retail investor or analyst with a free or paid screener.in account
Quarters to years: the ratios are public immediately, but acting on them requires patience most participants lack, which slows decay
A custom web-scraping or satellite pipeline you build in-house
Only your desk, until a vendor productizes the same feed
Months to years: decay accelerates sharply once the data becomes a licensed product any subscriber can buy

children.text: Not All 'Old Data' Alpha Is Actually Decaying

Here is the nuance an advanced researcher needs and a beginner course skips. Decay applies strongly to informational edges, being the first to know a fact. It applies far more weakly to structural or behavioral edges, being willing to do something most participants are psychologically or institutionally unable to do, even when the underlying data is completely public.

body.title: Informational Edge vs Structural or Behavioral Edge

columns.label: Informational Edge
points: Depends on knowing something before others do
Classic case: a short-lived pricing anomaly around a specific announcement
Decays fast once the data source or technique becomes common knowledge
This is the edge alternative data is chasing

columns.label: Structural or Behavioral Edge
points: Depends on doing something most participants will not or cannot do
Classic case: buying statistically cheap, out-of-favour Nifty 500 stocks and holding through the boredom
Persists even when the underlying data (P/E, P/B) is fully public, because few investors have the discipline or mandate to act on it consistently
This is why value and quality factors have kept working for decades despite being public knowledge

body.title: So why bother with alternative data at all, if behavioral edges already work?

children.text: Behavioral edges are real, but they tend to be slow, low Sharpe ratio, and capacity-constrained once too much systematic capital chases the same factor. A quant desk that wants a return stream with low correlation to standard factors, or that needs to act faster than a quarterly rebalance, has to find edges that are informational rather than behavioral. Alternative data is the search for fresh informational edges precisely because the traditional informational edges on price, volume, and reported financials have already been competed away by decades of quant participation in Indian and global markets.

The two are not mutually exclusive. A strong desk often runs a slow behavioral factor sleeve alongside a faster, higher-turnover alternative data sleeve, and Chapter 5 covers how to combine the two without one cannibalizing the other's risk budget.

body.title: Informational or Structural?
body.question: A quant fund's strategy is to systematically buy Nifty 500 stocks trading at the bottom decile of trailing P/B, rebalanced quarterly, and it has kept producing modest excess returns for over a decade despite the ratios being fully public on screener.in. What kind of edge is this most likely to be?
options: An informational edge that has somehow resisted decay
A structural or behavioral edge, since it depends on discipline to hold unpopular stocks rather than on private information
Not a real edge, since P/B is public data
A data processing edge from cleaning the P/B numbers better than screener.in
body.explanation: The data is fully public and has been for decades, so this cannot be an informational edge in the alternative-data sense. It persists because most investors are behaviorally or institutionally unwilling to consistently hold statistically cheap, unloved stocks through long stretches of underperformance. That discipline, not secret information, is the edge.

body.text: Before you pay for any alternative dataset, ask which kind of edge you are actually trying to build. If the answer is 'being early,' expect a high lambda and plan to keep sourcing new data every few quarters. If the answer is 'doing what others won't,' you may not need new data at all, you need discipline and the risk capacity to hold a public, unpopular position.

points: An edge can be modeled as decaying exponentially, R(t) = R0 x e^(-lambda x t), where lambda rises with how crowded and easily replicated a signal is
Traditional NSE and BSE data (price, volume, quarterly ratios) tends to sit on a steep decay curve because algorithmic trading and wide retail access to the same tools push lambda up quickly
A custom alternative data pipeline can sit on a much shallower curve, but only until a vendor turns the same feed into a licensed product any subscriber can buy
Decay applies mainly to informational edges (being first to know); structural or behavioral edges (doing what others won't) can persist for decades even on fully public data
Alternative data research specifically targets informational edges, since traditional informational edges have already been competed away by decades of quant participation
A well-built desk often separates a slow behavioral factor sleeve from a faster alternative-data sleeve rather than expecting one dataset to do both jobs
